meta.title: Sign-in with OAuth 2.0 + PKCE
meta.description: Authorization code flow with PKCE and OpenID Connect: who calls whom, in order, from the first click to the first API call.

summary.headline: The browser only ever carries a one-time code; tokens are exchanged on the back channel and bound to the app by the PKCE verifier.
points: The app sends a hashed challenge up front and proves it with the verifier at /token
The state parameter ties the callback to the session that started the login
Tokens never pass through the browser; the app keeps them server-side
The resource API checks the access token's signature, audience and expiry on every call

data.title: App backend
data.subtitle: Confidential OAuth client
data.description: Starts the login, creates the PKCE verifier and state, exchanges the code and keeps tokens in the server-side session.

data.title: Browser
data.subtitle: User agent, front channel
data.description: Follows redirects and holds only the session cookie. It never sees the access or refresh token.

data.title: Authorization server
data.subtitle: OpenID Provider
data.description: Authenticates the user, records consent, issues the one-time code and later the ID and access tokens.

data.title: Resource API
data.subtitle: Profile and account data
data.description: Accepts only access tokens with its own audience, checked against the provider's published keys.

steps.title: The user clicks Sign in
steps.description: The browser asks the app to start a login (GET /login). Nothing has been sent to the identity provider yet.

steps.title: The app redirects with a PKCE challenge
steps.description: The app creates a random code_verifier and state, stores both in the session, and redirects to /authorize with code_challenge = SHA-256(verifier).

steps.title: The user signs in at the provider
steps.description: The browser follows the redirect. The provider authenticates the user (password, passkey or SSO) and asks for consent to the requested scopes.

steps.title: A one-time code comes back
steps.description: The provider redirects to the app's registered callback with a short-lived authorization code and the original state. The browser delivers both to the app.

steps.title: Back-channel code exchange
steps.description: The app checks state, then posts the code, its client credentials and the code_verifier to /token. The provider recomputes the challenge and rejects any mismatch.

steps.title: Tokens are issued
steps.description: The provider returns an ID token (who the user is) and an access token (what the app may call), plus a refresh token if offline_access was granted.

steps.title: The app validates the ID token
steps.description: Signature against the provider's JWKS, issuer, audience, expiry and nonce. Only then is the user considered signed in.

steps.title: The browser gets a session cookie
steps.description: The app stores the tokens server-side and sets an HttpOnly, SameSite session cookie. The browser never holds a token.

steps.title: The app calls the API
steps.description: The app sends the access token as a Bearer header. The API verifies signature, audience, scope and expiry, then returns the profile.
